notes: New edge connection window: it shows the monitors of both PCs, one color per PC, with a notebook icon on built-in screens.
Drag a PC to arrange it: it always sticks to the other PC and aligns to the start, center or end of the neighboring monitor.
The touching edges are highlighted in full, and an animated pointer shows where the switch happens.
Edge switching now works on any monitor, not just the primary. Using another monitor of the controlled PC requires version 0.7.0 on that PC too.
The edge buttons in the main window were replaced by a summary and a Configure button, and the option to connect through the edge moved to the new window.

New option, off by default, to connect through the screen edge: touching this PC's edge connects to the recognized machine as the shortcut does, and hands over control once the connection is accepted.

After disconnecting with the button, touching the edge does not reconnect until you connect again by shortcut or in the app. With the machine unavailable, edge attempts happen at most every 5 seconds.
When an antivirus blocks or quarantines Winput LAN, the module page says so and explains how to restore it, instead of only stopping.
Winput LAN starts again on its own once the file is restored from quarantine, with no SwissTechKnife restart.
If an antivirus removes only one of the two copies of the app, the module starts the remaining one.
Disabling the module or closing SwissTechKnife while Winput LAN was exiting no longer raises an internal error.
Double-clicking the module's notification-area icon opens the Winput LAN window.
First release as a SwissTechKnife module: starts with SwissTechKnife in its own process, without a notification-area icon.
Settings, known machines and this PC's identity are copied from the regular installation on first run.
Allowing control of administrator apps asks for Windows confirmation once; afterwards the module starts with that permission.
The regular Winput LAN and the module never run at the same time.
